{{short description|Result pertaining to division rings}}
In [[abstract algebra]], the '''Cartan&ndash;Brauer&ndash;Hua theorem''' (named after [[Richard Brauer]], [[Élie Cartan]], and [[Hua Luogeng]]) is a theorem pertaining to [[division ring]]s. It says that given two division rings {{nowrap|''K'' ⊆ ''D''}} such that ''xKx''<sup>−1</sup> is contained in ''K'' for every ''x'' not equal to 0 in ''D'', either ''K'' is contained in the [[Center (ring theory)|center]] of ''D'', or {{nowrap|1=''K'' = ''D''}}.  In other words, if the [[unit group]] of ''K'' is a [[normal subgroup]] of the unit group of ''D'', then either {{nowrap|1=''K'' = ''D''}} or ''K'' is central {{harv|Lam|2001|p=211}}.
